ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, during the process in which a bar magnet approaches a closed metal ring from left to right, viewed from left to right, in what direction does the induced current in the ring flow?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a bar magnet, with the left end marked S and the right end marked N; on the right side of the magnet there is a closed metal ring. The velocity arrow v above the magnet points to the right, indicating that the magnet approaches the metal ring from left to right, and that the pole facing the metal ring is the N pole. Reasoning: The magnetic field lines outside the N pole start from the N pole, so at the metal ring, the direction of the magnetic field produced by the magnet is along the axis from left to right. As the magnet approaches the metal ring, the rightward magnetic flux through the surface of the ring increases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should hinder this increase in magnetic flux, so the induced magnetic field should be from right to left. When viewing the metal ring from left to right, a magnetic field from right to left is a magnetic field pointing toward the observer; according to the right-hand rule, the current in the ring should be in the counterclockwise direction.
